conventions.units: metres, real-world scale (glTF); Unreal glTF/Interchange import converts to cm automatically
conventions.axes: All facings are given in Blender space (Z-up, front = -Y unless stated). The glTF files are Y-up; the Unreal glTF importer converts back to Z-up - check the yaw of one asset after import (a 90/180 deg yaw offset may be needed) and apply the same correction to all.
conventions.custom_models: origin bottom-centre unless noted; transforms applied; weighted custom normals; plain placeholder materials named per slot (replace in Unreal)

polyhaven_models.notes: 3-masted Dutch galleon/fluyt, high carved stern castle, weathered dark timber, sails mostly furled with a few ragged/partly set; reads as an old anchored/derelict ship. Hull extends ~1.9 m below z=0 (origin ~ waterline). Best "old ship" pick.
Same hull/rig as dutch_ship_large_01 but modelled along Y with more sails set (light canvas). Use as a sailing variant. ~1.9 m below z=0.
Smaller 3-masted Dutch ship, same style/condition as the large ones, sails partly furled. ~2 m below z=0. Good for mid-distance/background fleet.
Largest and heaviest: full-rigged 3-masted ship with all sails set, darker hull, ornate stern galleries, intact condition. ~2.4 m below z=0. Hero ship / ghost-ship candidate (168k tris, 7 meshes).
